entities.summary: Henry Benedict Thomas Edward Maria Clement Francis Xavier Stuart, Cardinal Duke of York, also known as the Cardinal of York, was a cardinal, and was the third and final Jacobite heir to publicly claim the thrones of Great Britain and Ireland, as the younger grandson of King James VII and II. One of the longest-serving cardinals in history, Henry spent his whole life in the Papal States and became the dean of the College of Cardinals and cardinal-bishop of Ostia and Velletri. Unlike his father James Francis Edward Stuart and elder brother Charles Edward Stuart, Henry made no effort to seize the thrones.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a cardinal and member of the Stuart dynasty, Henry Benedict Stuart played a crucial role in maintaining the Catholic Church's influence during the Jacobite Risings, ultimately shaping the course of European politics and the balance of power between Catholicism and Protestantism.
